Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 6) demonstrates a small, hypoplastic right lung with diffuse opacity and a distinct rightward shift of the mediastinum and heart (dextroposition), which are hallmark features of Scimitar syndrome. While the classic "scimitar" vein is best seen on the CT scans (Figures 4 and 5), option B correctly describes the characteristic plain film findings of right lung hypoplasia and ipsilateral mediastinal shift associated with this condition.
